# Wickra

> Documentation for Wickra — streaming-first technical indicators with one Rust core and Python, Node, WASM, C ABI, and .NET bindings. Every indicator updates in O(1) constant time per tick, and the same code runs for backtesting and live ticks. The native packages are install-free — no C toolchain required.

Wickra implements each indicator once in Rust as a state machine, then re-exports that single implementation to Python (PyO3), Node (napi-rs), the browser (wasm-bindgen), and Rust itself, plus a C ABI (cbindgen) that any C-capable language — C, C++, Go, C#, Java, R — links against. Batch and streaming evaluation are guaranteed to produce identical output, pinned by reference-value tests. Dual-licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0.

## Start here
- [Overview](https://docs.wickra.org/overview): What Wickra is, how the core and bindings fit together, and the currently published versions.
- [Indicators overview](https://docs.wickra.org/Indicators-Overview): The full catalogue of indicator families, each linking to a per-indicator deep dive.

## Quickstarts
- [Rust](https://docs.wickra.org/Quickstart-Rust): Add the crate and stream your first indicator.
- [Python](https://docs.wickra.org/Quickstart-Python): `pip install wickra` and a streaming RSI example.
- [Node](https://docs.wickra.org/Quickstart-Node): `npm install wickra` and a streaming RSI example.
- [WASM](https://docs.wickra.org/Quickstart-WASM): Run indicators in the browser via WebAssembly.
- [C](https://docs.wickra.org/Quickstart-C): Link the generated `wickra.h` + library from C, C++ or any C-capable language.
- [C#](https://docs.wickra.org/Quickstart-CSharp): `dotnet add package Wickra` and idiomatic .NET indicator classes over the C ABI.
- [Go](https://docs.wickra.org/Quickstart-Go): `go get` the cgo binding and idiomatic Go indicator types over the C ABI.
- [R](https://docs.wickra.org/Quickstart-R): install the `.Call` binding and idiomatic R indicator constructors over the C ABI.

## Reference
- [Warmup periods](https://docs.wickra.org/Warmup-Periods): How many bars each indicator needs before it emits a value.
- [Streaming vs batch](https://docs.wickra.org/Streaming-vs-Batch): What the batch/streaming equivalence guarantee actually means.
- [Indicator chaining](https://docs.wickra.org/Indicator-Chaining): Feeding one indicator's output into another.
- [Data layer](https://docs.wickra.org/Data-Layer): Candles, sources, and the optional Binance WebSocket adapter.

## Guides
- [Cookbook](https://docs.wickra.org/Cookbook): Task-oriented recipes for common workflows.
- [TA-Lib migration](https://docs.wickra.org/TA-Lib-Migration): Moving from TA-Lib to Wickra.
- [FAQ](https://docs.wickra.org/FAQ): Common questions and answers.

## Source and packages
- [GitHub](https://github.com/wickra-lib/wickra): Source, issues, and releases.
- [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/wickra): Rust crate.
- [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/wickra/): Python package.
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/wickra): Node package.
- [Marketing site](https://wickra.org/): Live demo and benchmarks.
